To determine the default color level for a new Chalk instance, we need to look at the `readme.md` file, which states: "Color support is automatically detected based on the environment." This means that if no specific level is provided when creating a new Chalk instance, it will use the default level detected by the environment.

To override this default level, you can pass the `level` property when creating a new Chalk instance [C1:122-143]. For example, to create a new Chalk instance with level 0 (all colors disabled), you would use the following code:

```js
import {Chalk} from 'chalk';
const customChalk = new Chalk({level: 0});
```

This will create a new Chalk instance with level 0, effectively disabling all color support [C1:122-143].

items.answer: To render rgb and hex colours on terminals that only support 16 or 256 colours, Chalk uses the `ansiStyles` object to define the appropriate escape codes for each color model. The `ansiStyles.rgb` and `ansiStyles.hex` objects contain the necessary escape codes to set the text color or background color, respectively [C1:61-78]. When the terminal supports 16 or 256 colours, Chalk uses these escape codes to render the colors as expected [C1:36-61].
